Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. The umpires and the players are out in the middle followed by the West Indies openers - Brandon King and Kyle Mayers. Moeen Ali has the new ball in hand. Lets go...
...THE RUN CHASE...
Right then, West Indies have their task cut out if they are to chase this down. Can they do it? We shall find out in a bit. Join us for the second essay shortly.

Liam Livingstone is in for a quick chat. He says that he feels good to be in the T20 and the platform as set well. Adds that it feels good to get the team to such a big score. The pitch is a bit slow and they have a good score. Ends by saying that they will look to win this one.

West Indies had no answers to the assault from England. All the bowlers were taken to the cleaners. Only Hosein and Mayers had an economy of under 10 while the rest all went at over 12 runs to the over. Hosein, Holder, and Russell chipped in with one each but overall the bowlers had an off day.

England have been absolutely brutal in this innings and have posted a mammoth score of 267 for 3 after batting first. Having been put in, Buttler and Salt continued from where they left off in the last game and blasted the Windies bowlers all around the park. They added 117 for the opening wicket inside 10 overs. Buttler was dismissed for 55 but Salt carried on and made yet another ton as he got to 119 off just 57 with 10 maximums. Jacks and Livingstone also played their part and took England past the 260-run mark.

FOUR! Streaky but they all count! Full and outside off, Liam Livingstone throws a kitchen sink at it. Gets an outside edge as the ball finds the third man fence. West Indies end their innings for 267/3.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the game to begin. The umpires have made their way out in the middle. West Indies players are seen in a huddle, near the ropes. Jos Buttler and Phil Salt are the openers for England. Matthew Forde, the debutant, has the new ball in hand and will begin the proceedings. Let's go...

PITCH REPORT - Ian Bishop shares that there are some cracks in the middle, and it can be tricky for the batters. Adds that it seems to be a good track for bowling. Mentions that the spinners will hold the key and bowling in the right areas will be rewarding for the bowlers.

Jos Buttler the skipper of England says that they would have bowled as well. Adds that the wicket is good and they would have loved to chase. Says that they need to execute their plans well and level the series. Ends by mentioning the changes in their side.

Rovman Powell the skipper of West Indies says that they will bowl first. Adds that chasing gives them pleasure. Mentions the change as Alzarri Joseph misses out and Matthew Forde is making his debut today. Ends by saying that they will look to restrict England on a low score and win this game.

West Indies (Playing XI) - Brandon King, Shai Hope, Nicholas Pooran (WK), Sherfane Rutherford, Rovman Powell (C), Gudakesh Motie, Andre Russell, Jason Holder, Akeal Hosein, Matthew Forde (In for Alzarri Joseph), Kyle Mayers.

England (Playing XI) - Jos Buttler (C)(WK), Phil Salt, Will Jacks, Liam Livingstone, Harry Brook, Moeen Ali, Sam Curran, Chris Woakes (In for Tymal Mills), Rehan Ahmed (In for Gus Atkinson), Adil Rashid, Reece Topley.
TOSS - West Indies have won the toss and will BOWL first.

While the West Indies still have a lead in the series, they need to improve their bowling to prevent England from leveling the series. Can they do it? Or will the visitors make it 2-2? We shall find out together. Toss and team news to follow shortly...

Hello and a warm welcome to the 4th T20I between the West Indies and England. The series as of now stands with the hosts leading 2-1. The visitors won the last T20I against the West Indies in a high-scoring match, with Phil Salt scoring a century and Harry Brook hitting 24 runs in the last over. The West Indies bowled well in the first two matches but failed to contain England in the last few overs in the third match, resulting in a loss.
... MATCH DAY ...

It is now time for the 4th T20I between West Indies and England as the action now switches to the Brian Lara Stadium in Tarouba, Trinidad. The hosts had a 2-0 lead going into the 3rd T20I and once they put 222 runs on the board, it seemed like they would win the series with a couple of games to spare thanks to a brilliant 82 from Nicholas Pooran and a few superfast cameos from skipper Rovman Powell, Sherfane Rutherford and Jason Holder. However, England had other plans and after being under immense pressure to keep the series alive, the opening pair of captain Jos Buttler and Phil Salt put on a show for the spectators. They kept up with the required rate but lost a couple of wickets at the wrong time. Salt, who was cramping due to the heat, pulled off something remarkable and pummeled the bowling to bring up a sensational ton. But it was Harry Brook who just came in and struck 24 runs in five deliveries of the final over to pull off a grand heist and keep the visitors in with a chance to win the series. Both teams will look to tighten their bowling and the hosts might have to turn to someone else to bowl at the death as Andre Russell yet again went for plenty in the final over. The hosts still have the advantage and a win here will do the job for them. As for England, that run chase might have just galvanized the side and they will certainly be looking to level it all up and make the final match a decisive one. Who are you backing to get the win?
